title: 15-Minute Inspection Readiness Sweep
body:
## 15-Minute Inspection Readiness Sweep

Use for a surprise internal drill or immediately before an expected inspection. Do not use it as a substitute for the daily program.

- ☐ PIC/manager present and knows open food-safety issues.
- ☐ Employees with illness concerns are not handling food in violation of policy.
- ☐ Hand sinks stocked, accessible, clean, and functioning.
- ☐ Employees actively washing hands and changing gloves correctly.
- ☐ Cold foods ≤ 41°F; hot foods ≥ 135°F; thermometers available.
- ☐ No unsafe cooling/reheating condition in progress.
- ☐ Raw foods separated from ready-to-eat foods; correct shelf order.
- ☐ All stored prepared/open product has Muriale’s date + initials tape.
- ☐ No expired, unlabeled, leaking, damaged, or obviously spoiled food.
- ☐ Sanitizer prepared/tested correctly; wiping cloths controlled.
- ☐ Food-contact surfaces/equipment visibly clean and sanitized.
- ☐ Dish area set correctly; clean wares air drying; no cross-traffic contamination.
- ☐ Chemicals labeled and stored away from food/food-contact items.
- ☐ Floors/drains/walls/equipment free of obvious buildup; no leaks/sewage/standing water.
- ☐ No pest evidence; exterior/service doors controlled.
- ☐ Trash/dumpster/grease areas under control.
- ☐ Temperature, cleaning, corrective-action and training records available.
- ☐ Any problem found is being corrected now—not ignored.

The best inspection program is the one employees can see in the way the kitchen operates every day.
source: Health Inspection Success Program, Appendix E

title: Inspection-Day Response
body:
## Inspection-Day Response

**Rule:** Do not hide, falsify, back-date, move, or manufacture records for an inspection. Correct real conditions, answer accurately, provide requested records, and document the inspector's findings for follow-up.

- ☐ Notify the manager/PIC and Kitchen Operations Manager when the inspector arrives.
- ☐ Have one knowledgeable manager accompany the inspector when appropriate.
- ☐ Keep normal safe operations running; do not create chaos by overreacting.
- ☐ Correct simple conditions immediately when allowed and practical.
- ☐ Record every inspector finding, location, item involved, and any correction made.
- ☐ Ask for clarification when a finding or required correction is not understood.
- ☐ Collect the inspection report and any supporting documents before the visit is closed.
- ☐ Enter all follow-up items into the Corrective Action system and assign owners/dates.
- ☐ Conduct a brief post-inspection management review the same day or next business day.
